Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

as long as conjunction

provided that, on condition that

also provided that, providing, so long as, on condition that, if only (on condition)

classical

Cic. Off. 1.97: ōderint, dum metuant (Accius, quoted by Cicero; Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 5.4: id faciat saepe, dum nē lassus fīat

dum, dummodo (+ subjunctive)

conjunction, with the subjunctive; negative dum nē, dummodo nē

provided that, as long as

The condition on which the main clause holds. The negative is nē, not nōn.

Other words

  • modo (+ subjunctive) — if only, provided

    adverb, with the subjunctive; modo nē, modo ut · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. modo

    “Only let …”: the lighter form; see only.

Examples

  • ōderint, dum metuant

    let them hate, as long as they fearCic. Off. 1.97 (Lewis & Short)

  • opus rūsticum omne cūret utī sciat facere, et id faciat saepe, dum nē lassus fīat

    let him make sure he knows how to do every job on the farm, and do it often, as long as he doesn’t tire himselfCato Agr. 5.4

See also as long as, if, only.
